profile.name: Kibrom Abebe
profile.title: Full-Stack Software Engineer
profile.tagline: Building resilient web applications, scalable backends, and modular systems — from ARM assembly to cloud-deployed microservices.
profile.bio: I'm a passionate Full-Stack Software Engineer and student leader at Mekelle University, Ethiopia. I architect end-to-end digital solutions — spanning React + Next.js frontends, NestJS/Express microservice backends, Flutter mobile apps, and even ARM Cortex-M3 embedded firmware. I lead teams, contribute to open source, and obsess over clean architecture, API-first design, and developer experience.

philosophyPrinciples.title: Clean Architecture & Scalable Systems
philosophyPrinciples.description: I treat architecture as a first-class citizen — separating concerns, inverting dependencies, and ensuring systems remain testable and evolvable as they grow.

philosophyPrinciples.title: API-First Design
philosophyPrinciples.description: Contracts before code. Every backend service I build starts with an OpenAPI spec, enabling parallel frontend/backend development and living documentation.

philosophyPrinciples.title: Performance & Accessibility
philosophyPrinciples.description: Speed and inclusivity are non-negotiable. I optimize for Core Web Vitals, instrument with tracing tools, and build UIs that work for every user.

projects.title: Tigray Resilient Medical Referral System (TRMS)
projects.tagline: Enterprise-grade clinical platform managing end-to-end inter-facility medical referrals across distributed healthcare networks in Tigray, with offline-first sync, RBAC, and real-time triage

metrics.label: User Roles
metrics.description: Domain-level RBAC covering System Admin, Facility Admin, Dept Head, Doctor, Liaison Officer, HEW

projects.problemStatement: Fragmented paper-based inter-facility referral processes in Tigray's healthcare system caused delays, data loss, and poor patient outcomes — especially across facilities with intermittent connectivity. The system needed to handle referral routing, triage prioritization, and auditable consent across distributed health centers with zero tolerance for data corruption.
projects.architectureDescription: React 19 (Vite) → REST API (NestJS / Clean Architecture) → PostgreSQL (TypeORM + UnitOfWork) + JWT / Passport Auth → Offline-First Sync Engine → Chart.js Analytics
